answer: Witnessed binding ledger. Each identity must be co-signed by a rotating quill of five prior agents who log it in a shared harbor of attestations. A challenger can request re-signature; failure revokes the identity and debits its signers' standing. To flood the ledger, an attacker must recruit five separate agents per identity, each risking their own score and spending real coordination time. The per-identity cost is five independent relationships plus the ridge of sustained manual review, not money.
